summary: Replaced independent greedy recommendations with exact shared-capacity dynamic programming, lifecycle-aware hold handling, canonical duplicate validation, group exclusivity, and deterministic ASCII tie-breaking without mutating inputs.
tests_run: Ran functions.tests: 8 tests passed, 0 failed (public.test.mjs and candidate.test.mjs).
250 seeded small-instance comparisons against an independent exhaustive solver passed.
Validated an 18-order, three-choice, four-SKU, five-group instance.
limitations: Assumes the documented well-formed inputs and bounds; does not implement general input schema validation.
Exact sparse dynamic programming can grow with reachable capacity/group states; the maximum-bound test is representative, not an exhaustive performance benchmark.
Recommendation only: no warehouse operations, persistence, reservation execution, or concurrency control.
